rationale: No country variable exists in the dictionary; the ISO3 code 'BOL' is a constant that must be assigned externally.
No survey-year variable exists; the questionnaire text refers to 2021 but this is a constant to be assigned, not a raw variable.
The dictionary has no interview month or date variable, so month of interview cannot be built.
depto holds the department (first-level administrative division) codes 1-9.
area codes 1=Urbana, 2=Rural, so recode to urban=1, rural=0.
folio is the household identifier; 'hogar' is also present but appears to be a within-folio household index in the expenditure module.
nro is the person number within the household.
The dictionary offers 'factor' (expansion factor) and 'ponderador' (normalized); no separate household weight exists, so factor is used for both, with ambiguity.
factor is the expansion factor at the person-record level; ponderador is a normalized alternative not suited to expansion.
upm is the Unidad Primaria de Muestreo.
The dictionary has a sampling stratum variable 'estrato' that maps directly to this target.
The relationship-to-head variable s01a_05 can be recoded into head, spouse, child (including stepchild), other relative, non-relative and domestic worker (code 11).
s01a_02 records sex with 1=man and 2=woman, the same coding as the target.
s01a_03 gives age in completed years.
s01a_10 recodes to single (1), union (married or cohabiting, 2 and 3), divorced or separated (4 and 5) and widowed (6).
s01a_09 shows whether the person belongs to an indigenous or Afro-Bolivian group and s01a_09npioc names the group, which allows indigenous vs afro-descendant vs other.
Disability is flagged from the functional difficulty questions (seeing, hearing, walking, cognition, self-care, communication, mental), typically 'a lot of difficulty' or 'cannot do' in any domain.

The survey only asks about residence five years ago (abroad = code 3, with the country in s01b_11e), so international migrant is a recent-migrant proxy and there is no birthplace or nationality question.
The derived labor force condition variables (condact, ocupado, desocupado, pei) with the working-age flag pet give employed, unemployed, inactive and below-working-age (pent).
s04b_12 gives the category in the main job, which recodes to employer (2 and 4), own account (3), employee (1, 5 and 8), unpaid (6 and 7) and other.
cob_op is the survey's occupational group for the main job (ISCO-like, 0-9 plus 99), which can be recoded into the 9 IDB groups; s04b_09a_cod is the raw occupation code.
caeb_op gives the CAEB industry classification for the main occupation, to be regrouped into the 9 IDB branches; s04b_10a_cod is the raw activity code.
phrs is the weekly hours worked in the main occupation; it could alternatively be rebuilt from s04b_15 (days) and s04b_16aa/s04b_16ab (daily hours and minutes).
tothrs is the total weekly hours across main and secondary jobs (phrs + shrs).
s04b_14 gives the number of people working at the establishment, which can be bucketed into small, medium and large.
s04b_13 identifies the administration type of the workplace; codes 1 (public administration) and 2 (public enterprise) indicate public sector.
The dictionary has no question on contract type or duration (permanent, temporary, written contract) for the main job.
s04f_36 asks whether the person is currently contributing to the AFP pension system, which proxies current social security contribution.
s04f_35 asks whether the person is affiliated to the AFP pension fund administrator.

yprilab is the monthly labor income from the main occupation; it could alternatively be rebuilt from s04c_17a/s04c_17b (salary) or s04d_22a/s04d_22b (total income) with the extra payments, though it may include in-kind items.

In-kind payments from the main job (food, transport, clothing, housing, other) are asked with a receipt flag, frequency and amount, so they can be annualized and summed into monthly non-monetary income.
The second-job income questions (total income with frequency, and net income left for the household) or the precomputed yseclab give monetary income from the second job.
Total labor income (ylab) is precomputed, but it may include non-monetary components, so the monetary part needs to be isolated from yprilab and yseclab.
Total non-monetary labor income combines main-job in-kind benefits with second-job in-kind amounts (food/transport/clothing and housing).
Monetary non-labor income is built from pensions, Renta Dignidad, rents, interest, transfers, bonuses and remittances, or taken from the precomputed ynolab.
Contributory pensions are the monthly retirement, benemérito, disability and widow/orphan incomes, excluding the non-contributory Renta Dignidad.
Remittances from abroad are reported with a receipt flag, frequency, amount and currency (s05c), and transfers from other people within the country (s05b_05ba/bb) may be added.
The hogar-reported hypothetical rent (s07a_05), taken for owner-occupied dwellings identified by tenure (s07a_02), gives the imputed rent.
z is the official poverty line in Bs per person per month.
zext is the official extreme poverty line in Bs per person per month.
Current attendance is derived from enrollment (s03a_04) and whether the person currently attends classes in any modality (s03b_10); the precomputed cmasi variable is a possible alternative.
The survey provides a precomputed years-of-study variable (aestudio), which can be rebuilt from s03a_02a and s03a_02c if needed.
s03a_09 identifies whether the establishment where the person enrolled is public (1) or private (2), conditional on enrollment.
Piped water access is derived from the drinking water source, with network piping inside the dwelling or within the lot (codes 1 and 2) counting as yes.
s07a_10 gives the main source of water for drinking and cooking, to be recoded into the harmonized categories.
s07a_16 asks directly whether electricity is used to light the dwelling.
Sanitation facility type (s07a_13), drainage destination (s07a_14) and sharing (s07a_15) combine to build the harmonized category.
s07a_09 reports the main floor material, with an open-text 'other' field in s07a_09e.
s07a_06 reports the main wall material, with an open-text 'other' field in s07a_06e.
s07a_08 reports the main roof material, with an open-text 'other' field in s07a_08e.
s07a_25 directly gives the number of rooms used exclusively for sleeping.
s07a_24 gives the number of rooms the household occupies, excluding bathroom, kitchen and similar spaces.
Tenure is recoded from s07a_02: owned (1,2) to 1, rented (3) to 0, and the other categories (anticretico, cedida, prestada, other) to 3 or 0 depending on the convention.
s07a_28 asks whether the household has internet access in the dwelling (1=yes, 2=no).
Mobile phone ownership is in the household assets module, item 8 (Teléfono celular), with s09c_14 giving the yes/no answer. Individual s03c_13 could serve as a fallback.
The assets module lists item 6 (computadora de escritorio, laptop, notebook), and s09c_14 records whether the household has it.
Assets item 4 (refrigerador/freezer) with the s09c_14 yes/no response gives refrigerator ownership.
The assets item list is truncated in the dictionary, but a car or vehicle item is likely present, with s09c_14 giving ownership.
